script.base: No spread or total is saved, so the book’s lead/points script is unknown and this is a form-plus-injury hypothesis only. Baker Mayfield is Out, so Tampa’s passing efficiency should fall and the offense should hub through Bucky Irving (40 carries, 180 yards, 4.5 YPC in three games) against a Green Bay front that allows 4.34 YPC and is without DTs Warren Brinson and Anthony Campbell. Green Bay is down G Aaron Banks and C Jacob Monk, and Tampa blitzes 46% against a Love offense at -0.28 EPA/dropback when blitzed, so GB’s deep shots (Golden 416 air yards, Watson 304) are more likely to stall than to produce a shootout. Expect a lower-event game with Irving as the TB touch-volume piece and the backup living short if he throws.
script.flip1: The market has Jalon Daniels at 33.5 rush yards versus a 9-yard sample in the pack. If that is a mobile replacement and TB stays on the ground with Irving, Chris Godwin’s targets never show up and the short-area over dies, while Kenny Gainwell still should not reach 27.5 rush-plus-receiving unless the backfield committee actually flips.
script.flip2: GB’s protection collapses, Love falls behind, and the TB backup is forced into a dropback chase. Dog-style extra dropbacks (spread not saved, so this is only a flip) revive deep shots to Egbuka (12.5 aDOT) and Hurst (19.2 aDOT). Godwin can still see volume in that chase, but a deep-only chase misses him; Gainwell’s under still holds unless dump-offs jump well past his 7.3 receiving yards per game.

TB’s real overlap is Irving (40 carries, 4.5 YPC) into GB’s 4.34 YPC front with two DTs out — noted, not bet, because his rush line 55.5 sits above the 45 and 46 games and the 89 looks fluky. Egbuka (20 targets, 250 air, 12.5 aDOT) attacks the explosive area GB has not given up; that under was considered and not carded because 63/16/62 still disagrees and no spread confirms a low-dropback script.

pre_mortem: It’s Monday and the card lost. Gainwell went over 27.5 because Irving was nicked or the backup checked it down to the second back all afternoon, and the coin-flip 27.5 line was the market correctly smelling that role change from a three-game sample that was never going to stay at 10-18. Godwin stayed under 26.5 because the Mayfield haircut was real: team passing yards fell about a third, his 25-yard game was the new normal, and Tampa either ran with Irving and a mobile backup or threw the chase shots to Egbuka (63 and 62 already happened in this regime’s prior games) instead of the 4.7-aDOT option. We also never saw a spread, a kickoff forecast, or the 90-minute inactives, so a Mayfield reversal or a Daniels rushing script was sitting outside the pack. The Godwin counter is close enough that it stays a lean, not a strong; Gainwell’s counter needs a role change the carry split (40 to 10) does not show, so the under read still holds.
slip_story: One TB shrinkage story, not a shootout stack: with Mayfield out, featured non-Irving yardage is overpriced and what remains of the pass game is short. Gainwell rush+rec under 27.5 is the usage anchor and survives a run script or a pass script. Godwin receiving over 26.5 is the correlated short-area piece and is script-dependent — it loses if the backup only runs. Do not add Egbuka/Hurst overs, a total over, or Irving rush over to this slip; those need the opposite script. No parlay is placed.
